chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Yaqub ibn Salim, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and Al-A'ala ibn Kamil said to him, 'So-and-so does this to me and does that to me. If you see fit, supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is weakness with you. Say:'

O Allah, indeed You suffice from every thing, and nothing suffices from You, so suffice me from the matter of so-and-so with whatever You will, and however You will, and from wherever You will, and whenever You will.

key_terms.فُلَاناً: So-and-so (a placeholder for a specific person)
key_terms.يَفْعَلُ بِي: Does to me (implies action/behavior towards the speaker)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for seeking Allah's sufficiency against an enemy?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the common tendency to seek specific, targeted divine intervention by teaching a comprehensive supplication for sufficiency (*kafāyah*). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *al-kifāyah*—trusting Allah to handle the matter in the most beneficial way, whether through removal, humiliation, or protection, rather than limiting God's wisdom to a single outcome. The Imam’s advice underscores the spiritual maturity of accepting Allah’s decree (*mashī’ah*) over rigid demands for specific results.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymi, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Yaqoub Bin Salim who said, 
‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-A’ala Bin Kamil said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So and so goes against me, and goes against me. So if you<sup>asws</sup> view proper, you<sup>asws</sup> could supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is weakness with you. Say, 
‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> Suffice me from everything and nothing can suffice from You<sup>azwj</sup>, therefore Suffice me with the matter of so and so with whatever You<sup>azwj</sup> so Desire to, and from wherever You<sup>azwj</sup> so Desire to, and whenever You<sup>azwj</sup> so Desire to’’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan al-Taymi from Ali ibn Asbat from Ya’qub ibn Salim who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and al-‘Ala’ ibn Kamil said to him, ‘So and so acts against me again and again, if you consider it proper, pray to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy.’ The Imam said, ‘This is more than enough for you. Say,

“O Lord, You are sufficient for everything and nothing is sufficient for You. Suffice me in the matters of so and so with whatever You wish, in whatever way You wish, from wherever You wish and whenever You wish.’”
